easy.explanation: The verse says, “My son, forget not my law.”
easy.q: What does the father tell his son not to forget?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “let thine heart keep my commandments.”
easy.q: What is the son told to keep in his heart?

easy.explanation: Verse 3 says, “Let not mercy and truth forsake thee.”
easy.q: What should not forsake the son?

answers: Length of days, long life, and peace
medium.explanation: Verse 2 names length of days, long life, and peace.
medium.q: What blessings are connected with keeping the commandments?

answers: Upon the table of the heart
medium.explanation: The verse says, “write them upon the table of thine heart.”
medium.q: Where should mercy and truth be written?

medium.explanation: Verse 4 promises favour and good understanding in the sight of God and man.
medium.q: What will a person find by keeping mercy and truth?

answers: They should become visible and deeply internalized
They are needed only during worship
They belong only in written books
challenge.explanation: The two images point to a constant outward and inward commitment.
challenge.q: What does binding mercy and truth around the neck and writing them on the heart suggest?

challenge.explanation: Verse 4 says, “in the sight of God and man.”
challenge.q: Who are said to see the favour and good understanding of the faithful person?

answers: Keeping the law, preserving mercy and truth, and receiving peace and favour
Pursuing wealth, gaining power, and winning battles
Learning trade, building barns, and planting vineyards
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from obedience to character and then to blessing.
challenge.q: What progression appears in verses 1–4?

paragraphs.title: Trust in God and Turning from Evil

easy.explanation: Verse 5 says, “Trust in the LORD with all thine heart.”
easy.q: In whom should a person trust?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “lean not unto thine own understanding.”
easy.q: What should a person not lean upon?

easy.explanation: Verse 7 says, “fear the LORD, and depart from evil.”
easy.q: From what should a person depart?

answers: He will direct the person’s paths
medium.explanation: Verse 6 promises, “he shall direct thy paths.”
medium.q: What does acknowledging the LORD in all one’s ways bring?

answers: Do not rely exclusively on personal judgment
Do not walk on a road
medium.explanation: The command warns against depending only on one’s own understanding.
medium.q: What does “lean not unto thine own understanding” mean?

answers: Health and marrow to the bones
medium.explanation: Verse 8 describes this way as health and marrow to the bones.
medium.q: What is promised to the person who fears the LORD and departs from evil?

answers: Trust the LORD rather than relying only on personal understanding
Trust human strength above all else
challenge.explanation: The passage does not forbid understanding; it forbids relying on it alone.
challenge.q: What balance do these verses teach concerning trust and understanding?

answers: He will cease from all activity
challenge.explanation: Divine direction is the explicit promise of verse 6.
challenge.q: What may change when someone acknowledges the LORD in every way?

answers: They are described as health and strength to the body
They are described as a disease
They have no connection with the body
challenge.explanation: Verse 8 uses bodily images: health to the navel and marrow to the bones.
challenge.q: How are fear of the LORD and turning from evil connected with health?

easy.explanation: Verse 9 says, “Honour the LORD with thy substance.”
easy.q: With what should a person honour the LORD?

easy.explanation: The verse calls for “the firstfruits of all thine increase.”
easy.q: What should be given from one’s increase?

answers: They will be filled with plenty
They will be turned into houses
easy.explanation: Verse 10 says, “thy barns be filled with plenty.”
easy.q: What will happen to the barns?

answers: Substance and the firstfruits of increase
medium.explanation: The passage mentions substance and the firstfruits of all increase.
medium.q: What does the giving described in these verses include?

answers: They will burst out with new wine
medium.explanation: Verse 10 says, “thy presses shall burst out with new wine.”
medium.q: What will happen to the presses?

answers: The first and best portion of the increase
medium.explanation: Firstfruits are the first portion of the harvest or increase.
medium.q: What does “firstfruits” mean in this passage?

answers: Giving honour to the LORD is followed by abundant barns and presses
The passage gives no connection between the two
challenge.explanation: The command to honour the LORD is followed by promises of agricultural abundance.
challenge.q: What relationship is presented between honouring God and abundance?

answers: Giving is not merely offering what remains
Giving should happen only after everything else is used
The quality of the gift does not matter
challenge.explanation: The word “firstfruits” places the gift at the beginning and gives it priority.
challenge.q: What does giving the firstfruits emphasize?

answers: Barns filled with plenty and presses bursting with new wine
challenge.explanation: These are the two agricultural images in the verse.
challenge.q: Which pair of results appears in verse 10?

paragraphs.title: Discipline, Rebuke, and the Praise of Wisdom

easy.explanation: Verse 11 says, “despise not the chastening of the LORD.”
easy.q: What should a son not despise?

answers: Because He loves the person He corrects
easy.explanation: Verse 12 connects correction with the LORD’s love.
easy.q: Why does the LORD correct?

easy.explanation: Verse 15 says, “She is more precious than rubies.”
easy.q: What is wisdom more precious than?

answers: As a father corrects the son in whom he delights
As a stranger rejects an enemy
As a king rewards a soldier
medium.explanation: Verse 12 compares the LORD’s correction to a father correcting a beloved son.
medium.q: How is the LORD’s correction compared with a father’s correction?

medium.explanation: Verse 13 calls happy the man who finds wisdom and gets understanding.
medium.q: What does the happy man find?

answers: Life, riches, honour, pleasantness, and peace
medium.explanation: Verses 16–18 associate wisdom with these blessings.
medium.q: What benefits are associated with wisdom?

answers: Correction can be an expression of loving delight
Correction proves that love is absent
challenge.explanation: The fatherly comparison shows correction as connected with love.
challenge.q: What do these verses teach about the relationship between correction and love?

answers: Wisdom gives life and happiness to those who hold fast to her
Wisdom is only about studying nature
challenge.explanation: Verse 18 calls wisdom a tree of life to those who lay hold upon her.
challenge.q: What does the image “She is a tree of life” communicate about wisdom?

answers: She is more precious than rubies and also brings pleasantness and peace
She is difficult to obtain and therefore useless
challenge.explanation: The passage joins wisdom’s incomparable value with her peaceful benefits.
challenge.q: What contrast appears in the description of wisdom?

paragraphs.title: Wisdom as the Foundation of Creation

easy.explanation: Verse 19 says, “The LORD by wisdom hath founded the earth.”
easy.q: By what did the LORD found the earth?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “by understanding hath he established the heavens.”
easy.q: By what did He establish the heavens?

easy.explanation: Verse 20 says, “By his knowledge the depths are broken up.”
easy.q: What was broken up by His knowledge?

medium.explanation: Wisdom is linked with the earth, understanding with the heavens, and knowledge with the depths.
medium.q: Which three qualities are connected with creation?

medium.explanation: The verse says, “the clouds drop down the dew.”
medium.q: What do the clouds do in verse 20?

medium.explanation: To establish is to set up or make firm.
medium.q: What does “established” mean in “established the heavens”?

answers: Wisdom is presented as foundational to God’s work, not merely as practical advice
Wisdom has no connection with God’s actions
challenge.explanation: The verses connect wisdom, understanding, and knowledge with the formation of creation.
challenge.q: What does the connection between wisdom and creation teach?

answers: Earth by wisdom, heavens by understanding, and depths and dew by knowledge
Heavens by wealth, earth by honour, and dew by peace
Depths by mercy, earth by truth, and heavens by fear
challenge.explanation: This is the order in which the verse presents the divine qualities and works.
challenge.q: What sequence appears in verses 19–20?

answers: Both are presented as works of God’s knowledge
They are unrelated in the passage
challenge.explanation: Both appear under the statement, “By his knowledge.”
challenge.q: What connection exists between the depths and the dew?

easy.explanation: Verse 21 says, “let not them depart from thine eyes: keep sound wisdom and discretion.”
easy.q: What should not depart from the son’s eyes?

easy.explanation: Verse 23 says, “Then shalt thou walk in thy way safely.”
easy.q: How will the person walk?

easy.explanation: Verse 24 says, “thou shalt not be afraid.”
easy.q: What will the person not fear when lying down?

medium.explanation: Verse 22 says, “they be life unto thy soul.”
medium.q: What will sound wisdom and discretion be to the soul?

medium.explanation: The same verse says they will be “grace to thy neck.”
medium.q: What will wisdom and discretion be to the neck?

medium.explanation: Verse 24 says, “thy sleep shall be sweet.”
medium.q: What kind of sleep is promised?

answers: The LORD, who is the person’s confidence and protector
challenge.explanation: Verse 26 says, “the LORD shall be thy confidence.”
challenge.q: What is the source of confidence at the end of the passage?

answers: Sudden fear, the desolation of the wicked, and having one’s foot taken
challenge.explanation: The passage names several kinds of danger and promises protection from them.
challenge.q: Which dangers are mentioned in these verses?

answers: Keeping wisdom brings life to the soul and grace to the neck
The passage makes no connection between them
challenge.explanation: Verse 22 explicitly connects sound wisdom and discretion with life and grace.
challenge.q: What connection exists between keeping wisdom and grace?

easy.explanation: Verse 27 says, “Withhold not good from them to whom it is due.”
easy.q: What should not be withheld from those to whom it is due?

answers: “Go, and come again, and to morrow I will give”
easy.explanation: Verse 28 forbids delaying a gift that can be given at once.
easy.q: What should a person not say to his neighbour when he has the means to give?

answers: His neighbour who dwells securely by him
A stranger who is far away
easy.explanation: Verse 29 says, “Devise not evil against thy neighbour.”
easy.q: Against whom should a person not devise evil?

answers: When it is in the power of your hand to do it
medium.explanation: Verse 27 emphasizes that the ability to do good is already present.
medium.q: When should good not be delayed?

answers: Do not refuse to do a good thing for the person to whom it is due
Do not speak with other people
medium.explanation: The command concerns refusing or delaying rightful help.
medium.q: What does “withhold not good” mean?

answers: When that person has done you harm
medium.explanation: Verse 30 forbids striving without cause if the other person has done no harm.
medium.q: When does the passage allow striving with another person?

answers: Act justly and promptly, without withholding help or plotting harm
Avoid all relationships with other people
challenge.explanation: The commands promote honest, responsible, and peaceful treatment of others.
challenge.q: What principle unites the commands in verses 27–30?

answers: One gives a neighbour what is due, while the other plans to harm him
challenge.explanation: The verses contrast active goodness with secret harm.
challenge.q: What contrast exists between giving good and devising evil?

answers: Because the ability to help already exists today
Because only wealthy people may help
challenge.explanation: The verse says the needed good is already “by thee.”
challenge.q: Why is delaying help until tomorrow wrong in verse 28?

easy.explanation: Verse 31 says, “Envy thou not the oppressor.”
easy.q: Whom should a person not envy?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “choose none of his ways.”
easy.q: Whose ways should a person not choose?

easy.explanation: Verse 34 says, “he giveth grace unto the lowly.”
easy.q: To whom does the LORD give grace?

medium.explanation: Verse 32 says, “the froward is abomination to the LORD.”
medium.q: How does the LORD regard the froward?

answers: A person who is morally crooked or perverse
medium.explanation: The word describes someone turned away from what is right.
medium.q: What does “froward” describe?

answers: The wise inherit glory, and fools receive shame
The wise receive shame, and fools inherit glory
medium.explanation: Verse 35 contrasts glory for the wise with shame for fools.
medium.q: What do the wise inherit, and what do fools receive?

answers: The oppressor’s way is rejected, while the LORD’s secret and blessing are with the righteous
Both ways receive the same blessing
The oppressor’s way is presented as better
challenge.explanation: The passage warns against the oppressor and praises the righteous.
challenge.q: What central contrast appears between the oppressor’s way and the righteous way?

answers: His ways must not be chosen, and the LORD rejects the froward
challenge.explanation: The verse forbids both envy and imitation of the oppressor.
challenge.q: Why should a person not envy the oppressor, even if his ways seem attractive?

answers: The LORD is with the righteous, gives grace to the lowly, glory to the wise, and shame to fools
The wicked receive wealth, scorners receive grace, and fools receive honour
The righteous receive shame and fools receive wisdom
challenge.explanation: These four results summarize the final contrast between uprightness and wickedness.
challenge.q: Which sequence of moral results concludes the passage?
